issues_detected.description: The documented processing pipeline (node2vec, DenseNet-121, contrastive co-embedding, HiDeF community detection, GPT-4/Gene Set AI naming) produces predicted cell maps, and the record states explicitly in known_limitations that 'It does not contain predicted cell maps, which will be added in future releases.' No software is named for producing or transforming the files that are actually distributed (SEC-MS and AP-MS result archives, the Perturb-seq cell atlas, the immunofluorescence image archives). FAIRSCAPE is named only as the RO-Crate packaging and provenance-metadata framework.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name the software that produced each distributed file collection (for example the mass-spectrometry search and SEC elution-profile software, and the single-cell alignment/quantification software behind cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_cell_atlas.zip), with versions, alongside the cell-map pipeline whose outputs are not in this release.

issues_detected.description: Version numbering is internally inconsistent: this June 2026 release is recorded as version '2.0', while version_access lists the earlier June 2025 and October 2025 releases at version '2.1'; the citation string ends 'V2'. A later release carrying a lower version number than its predecessors will mislead automated version resolution.
issues_detected.recommendation: Reconcile the release version sequence (or state explicitly that Dataverse major version 'V2' and the CM4AI release label are distinct numbering systems).

issues_detected.description: No variable-level metadata is provided. The `variables` slot is absent entirely, so no data dictionary, column definitions, or identifiers exist for the tabular content inside the distributed SEC-MS, AP-MS and Perturb-seq archives.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add `variables` entries describing the columns of the mass-spectrometry and Perturb-seq result tables, with identifiers and units where applicable.

issues_detected.description: is_deidentified asserts a deidentification status and its rationale ('non-clinical (from tissue cultures) and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject') but names no deidentification method or standard. The rationale is semantically appropriate for immortalized and commercially sourced cell-line material, where no subject-level deidentification step was performed by the producers, but the record leaves the upstream basis unstated.
issues_detected.recommendation: State that deidentification was effected upstream by the cell-line providers (ATCC, HipSci) and cite the provider's deidentification or donor-consent basis, rather than asserting the status alone.

issues_detected.description: distribution_formats declares only the container format ('ZIP Archive', media_type application/zip) and the RO-Crate packaging standard. The formats of the files inside the archives (image format, mass-spectrometry table format, single-cell matrix format) and character encoding are not specified anywhere in the record.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add per-collection format and media_type entries for the archive contents (for example image/tiff, text/tab-separated-values, application/x-hdf5) and record character encoding for text files.

issues_detected.description: Neither `anomalies` nor `missing_data_documentation` is populated. cleaning_strategies records only that single-cell CRISPR screen data 'were reported as undergoing quality control at the time of the CM4AI preprint', without stating outcomes, exclusions, or known quality defects in the released files.
issues_detected.recommendation: Document known anomalies (failed antibodies, low-confidence elution profiles, dropped guides) and missing-data patterns per file collection, and update the cleaning status now that the release is published.

issues_detected.description: No errata and no per-release change description. `updates` documents cadence (quarterly through November 2026) but not what changed between the October 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM) and this one; the reader must diff the two records to learn what was added.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add release notes in updates.update_details enumerating additions, removals, and corrections relative to the immediately preceding release DOI.

issues_detected.description: The `download_url` slot is not populated; the platform access link is carried in distribution_formats.access_urls (https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C) with a note that the Data Access API is available. The information a consumer needs is present, but not in the slot a harvester would read.
issues_detected.recommendation: Mirror the Dataverse access URL into `download_url` so automated harvesters resolve it.

issues_detected.description: Temporal fields are non-monotonic in two places: created_on (2025-02-27) is flagged by the record's own source_caveats as a Dataverse value carried unchanged across four successive releases, and five immunofluorescence file collections are listed as published 2026-07-15, after the dataset issued date of 2026-06-17. Both are disclosed rather than concealed.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record a release-specific creation or modification date and note in distribution_dates that the image archives were added a month after the initial release publication.

issues_detected.description: Cell-line RRIDs (RRID:CVCL_0419 for MDA-MB-468, RRID:CVCL_B5P3 for KOLF2.1J) are valid Cellosaurus identifiers but appear only inside direct_collection prose, not in a resolvable identifier slot. No dataset-level RRID is claimed (none is required; the DOI serves that role).
issues_detected.recommendation: Expose the cell-line RRIDs as structured identifiers on the relevant subsets so they are machine-resolvable.

semantic_insights: DOI 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C is well formed and the 10.18130 prefix is the University of Virginia Dataverse, which matches publisher ROR:0153tk833 (University of Virginia) and the dataverse.lib.virginia.edu access URL — identifier, publisher and access path are mutually consistent.

NIH award strings follow expected NIH construction: 1OT2OD032742-01 and core project OT2OD032742 (Other Transaction, OD institute), the supplement 3OT2OD032742-01S2, and 5U54HG012513-02 for the Bridge2AI Bridge Center; the stated PI and organization match the creator list.

The human-subjects determination is coherent across the record and is evidenced outside Element 4: the description names cell lines (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J) rather than participants, collection_mechanisms describe instruments and laboratories rather than recruitment, and direct_collection.is_direct is false with an explicit statement that data were not collected from human subjects.

Governance is documented independently of human subjects: a named CM4AI Data Access Committee with a contact, two named ethics-review contacts with ORCIDs and institutional emails, and an access review process covering dual licensing for commercial use.

License, prohibited uses and IP restrictions are mutually reinforcing rather than merely repeated: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with data_use_permission no_commercial_use, a prohibition on commercial use, and named copyright holders (Regents of the University of California; Stanford for raw image data) with a route to separate licensing.

Bias disclosure is honest and specific to the data type: representation_bias scoped to the fact that commercially sourced cell lines 'do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large', with affected_subsets named.

Explicit negative flags (confidential_elements_present: false, sensitive_elements_present: false, content_warnings_present: false, hipaa_compliant: not_applicable, FDA Regulated: No) are accompanied by reasoning, so they function as documentation rather than as empty defaults.

The 464-proteins-per-condition figure is used consistently across instances, subpopulations.distribution and three immunofluorescence file_collections, and the record openly reconciles it against a conflicting 563 figure in an older release page.

Source provenance is layered and checkable: raw deposits in MassIVE, SRA via NCBI BioProject and Figshare; RO-Crate provenance graphs via FAIRSCAPE; and four prior release DOIs linked with is_new_version_of relationships.

The record's own source_caveats block flags several of the weaknesses an evaluator would otherwise have to infer (carried-over creation date, missing byte counts, inferred language and is_tabular, omitted collection timeframes), which is a mark of disciplined provenance reporting even though the underlying gaps remain.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
sub_elements.quality_note: A single persistent identifier is used consistently as the dataset id, the DOI, and the latest-version pointer, and subset ids are minted as fragments beneath it.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Matches 10.XXXX/... ; prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia Dataverse registrant, plausible for a dataset whose publisher is ROR:0153tk833 (University of Virginia) and whose access URL is dataverse.lib.virginia.edu. Valid.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description of ~1,900 characters naming the modalities (Perturb-seq, SEC-MS, AP-MS, immunofluorescence), the cell lines and treatment conditions, the RO-Crate/FAIRSCAPE packaging, the three-pillar/six-module organization, and the nine collaborating institutions
sub_elements.quality_note: Far beyond the 200-character threshold and substantively informative: a reader learns which modalities cover which cell lines and conditions before opening a file.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Description content matches the claimed dataset type (multi-modal proteomics/imaging/perturbation) and matches file_collections one-for-one. Consistent.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: 27 terms including AI, AP-MS, Bridge2AI, CM4AI, CRISPR/Cas9, KOLF2.1J, MDA-MB-468, perturb-seq, SEC-MS, paclitaxel, vorinostat, subcellular imaging
sub_elements.quality_note: Well above the five-keyword threshold and spans domain, method, cell line, reagent and program dimensions, including both spelled-out and abbreviated forms.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Every keyword is corroborated by content elsewhere in the record; no orphan or aspirational tags. Program context (Bridge2AI, CM4AI) is inferred from quoted keyword values only.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/; distribution_formats.access_urls: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; file_collections lists 10 named archives with paths, sizes and MD5 checksums; total_file_count: 10
sub_elements.quality_note: Both a project-level landing page and a repository record are given, and the resource structure is enumerated down to per-file checksums.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Both URLs are well formed with plausible domains; total_file_count (10) equals the number of file_collections entries. Consistent.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: six typed relationships — four is_new_version_of (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, F3TD5R, B35XWX, DXWOS5), one is_described_by (doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311), one is_referenced_by (doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734); subsets: seven subset ids beneath the dataset DOI
sub_elements.quality_note: The release lineage is fully navigable and each relationship carries a resolvable target DOI and a human-readable name; seven internal subsets give the within-dataset hierarchy.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: All target DOIs are well formed; the 10.1101 prefix correctly denotes bioRxiv preprints for the two literature relationships. parent_datasets is unused, but the is_new_version_of chain conveys the same lineage. Consistent.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: full CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 statement with attribution, non-commercial and share-alike conditions; data_use_permission: no_commercial_use; contact_person: Trey Ideker. ip_restrictions.restrictions: 'Copyright is held by the Regents of the University of California except where otherwise noted; spatial proteomics raw image data is copyright the Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University. Commercial use requires a separate license negotiation...'
sub_elements.quality_note: Actionable rather than boilerplate: it names the license, the per-package copyright holders, the excluded use, and a person to contact for a commercial licence.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: License, data_use_permission enum, prohibited_uses and ip_restrictions all state the same non-commercial restriction without contradiction. Consistent.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions: 'The release records FDA Regulated: No'; hipaa_compliant: not_applicable; regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact: Jillian Parker (ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486); data_governance.committee_name: CM4AI Data Access Committee, committee_contact and access_review_process; confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present: false with reasoning
sub_elements.quality_note: The regulatory determinations are negative but reasoned, and the record supplies both a named governance committee and a named contact with an institutional email — the governance-contact scope of this sub-element is met.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: hipaa_compliant: not_applicable is semantically correct for non-clinical cell-line proteomics; a HIPAA-compliant claim would have been the implausible answer here. No confidentiality_level enum value is set, which is the one gap. Consistent.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats.access_urls: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C with notes 'Individual files below the download size limit may be downloaded directly; the Data Access API is available for programmatic access'
sub_elements.quality_note: A resolvable repository link plus explicit instructions for both interactive and programmatic retrieval, including the size-limit caveat that matters for the 3.8-4.6 GB image archives.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The dedicated `download_url` slot is empty and the link lives in distribution_formats.access_urls; the sub-element asks for a direct link or platform access instructions and both are present, so the point is earned, with the slot placement recorded as a low-severity correctness issue.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: [format: 'ZIP Archive', media_type: application/zip], [format: 'RO-Crate']; file_collections: 10 entries each with compression: zip, a path, a size and an MD5; conforms_to: RO-Crate
sub_elements.quality_note: Container format, MIME type, compression and per-file checksums are all given, which is enough to retrieve and verify the distribution.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: media_type application/zip is the correct MIME type for the stated format. Only the container is described — the formats of the files inside the archives are nowhere stated — which is recorded as a low-severity completeness issue and constrains Element 3 rather than this retrieval-focused sub-element.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: 6 typed entries; external_resources: 11 entries including MassIVE deposits for iPSC and cancer-cell mass spectrometry, AP-MS deposits, SRA via NCBI BioProject, Figshare CRISPRi atlas, https://cm4ai.org, https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/, https://fairscape.github.io, http://integrativemodeling.org
sub_elements.quality_note: Unusually thorough: raw deposits, code, documentation and modelling software are all linked, and embargo status is attached to the one resource that is restricted.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: All URLs are well formed with plausible domains; archival: true flags distinguish permanent deposits from project pages. The embargo note on the Perturb-seq resource matches the integration_limitation in known_limitations. Consistent.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met on non-E3 evidence: distribution_formats is populated with a Dataverse access URL, file_collections enumerates 10 retrievable archives with checksums, and license CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 explicitly permits sharing and adaptation.
sub_elements.evidence: license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Users are free to share and adapt the material, provided appropriate credit is given, a link to the license is provided, changes are indicated, the material is not used for commercial purposes, and contributions are distributed under the same license'
sub_elements.quality_note: A named, standard, machine-recognisable license whose permissions and conditions are spelled out, plus a stated route to commercial licensing.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 is a real Creative Commons identifier and the paraphrase of its terms is accurate. Non-commercial and share-alike conditions limit but do not block reuse. Valid.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition as above, evidenced by distribution_formats, file_collections and the Dataverse access URL.
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: format 'ZIP Archive' with media_type application/zip; format 'RO-Crate' with notes 'CM4AI output data are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework'; conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]
sub_elements.quality_note: The distribution is packaged in an open, community-standard research-object format (RO-Crate, a JSON-LD profile) inside plain ZIP with a declared MIME type, so a consumer can unpack and interpret the package structure by standard tooling.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Partial: the packaging layer is standardised and correctly identified, but no inner file format and no character encoding are recorded anywhere in the record (raw_data_format says only 'Confocal microscopy image with four color channels'). Scored 1 on the strength of the RO-Crate/MIME declarations, with the missing inner formats raised as a low-severity completeness issue.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition as above.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances carry ontology-coded slots data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19 / B2AI_SUBSTRATE:63 and data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:15 / :26 / :12
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is asserted at three levels — packaging standard, metadata schema with a resolvable w3id URI, and class — and content-level annotation uses program ontology CURIEs rather than free text.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The w3id URI is well formed and the CURIE prefixes are used consistently. Cell-map annotation is separately stated to align to Gene Ontology and Reactome. Valid.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared condition as above; the sub-element is therefore scored rather than excluded, and the absence of `variables` is a score of 0 rather than a reason for exclusion (anti-circular rule).
sub_elements.evidence: No `variables` slot anywhere in the record. The nearest content is instances[].notes (image channel composition, gene counts) and file_collections[].description.
sub_elements.quality_note: A reuser cannot learn the columns, units or identifiers of the SEC-MS elution tables, the AP-MS interaction records, or the Perturb-seq atlas without downloading and inspecting the archives. This is the record's largest interoperability gap.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Absent field; not excusable by is_tabular: false, since the SEC-MS, AP-MS and Perturb-seq archives plainly contain tabular result files. Fails.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: 5 categories (AI-ready research data, AI model training, cellular process analysis, perturbation and disease-context analysis, bioinformatics analysis of component datasets); prohibited_uses: clinical decision-making without regulatory oversight, and commercial use; discouraged_uses: use without domain expertise, use as a complete cell-map resource
sub_elements.quality_note: All three registers are populated with reasons rather than labels, and the guidance is candid about what this interim release is not good for.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The prohibition on commercial use matches the CC BY-NC-SA license and ip_restrictions; the discouragement against treating this as a complete cell-map resource matches the scope_limitation in known_limitations. Consistent.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition FAILS on E1/E8 evidence: the description names cell lines (MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells, KOLF2.1J iPSCs) rather than participants or patients, keywords contain no participant/patient/clinical-research term, and collection_mechanisms (E8) describe SEC-MS, AP-MS, ICC-IF microscopy and CRISPRi screens rather than recruitment. The governance condition SUCCEEDS on E2 evidence: regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact names Jillian Parker as governance contact, and the E2 access-policy fields impose an applicable constraint (ip_restrictions require separate licence negotiation for commercial use). Per the per-sub-element gate, the governance disjunct opens sub-elements 1 and 2.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries — 'Ethical review for the CM4AI project is led by the Ethics Module, which developed a plan for ethical preparation, licensing, dissemination, and Data Access supervision of CM4AI datasets, balancing openness of the data produced with protection of intellectual property...' (contact Vardit Ravitsky, ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801, ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org) and a second review contact (Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon, Simon Fraser University). data_governance: CM4AI Data Access Committee with committee_contact, access_review_process and stewardship_roles. human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: false with reasoning on ethically sourced lines (ATCC; HipSci MTA).
sub_elements.quality_note: Oversight is described as a standing function with named, contactable people and a stated remit (licensing, dissemination, data-access supervision), not as a one-line assertion. Appropriate to a dataset with governance but no participants.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Consistency check: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=false, so no IRB protocol number is expected and none is demanded. data_protection_impacts is absent, which is defensible where no personal data are processed. The ethics-review contacts named here also satisfy Element 9 sub-element 5. Consistent.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same determination as sub-element 1: human-subjects condition fails on E1/E8 evidence; governance condition succeeds on E2 evidence (regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact; commercial-use constraint in ip_restrictions). Deidentification is meaningful for donor-derived cell-line material even without participants.
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; is_deidentified.deidentification_details: 'The release records De-identified Samples: Yes. CM4AI data are distinctive within Bridge2AI in that they are non-clinical (from tissue cultures) and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.' Corroborated by direct_collection: 'commercially available, de-identified human cell lines: MDA-MB-468 (RRID:CVCL_0419), available from ATCC, and KOLF2.1J (RRID:CVCL_B5P3), available from the HipSci resource.'
sub_elements.quality_note: The record states the deidentification status, the basis for it (tissue-culture material with no linkage to a subject under current knowledge), the sourcing of both lines, and the residual-knowledge caveat. For immortalized and donor-derived lines that is the semantically appropriate answer.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Method appropriateness: naming HIPAA Safe Harbor, Expert Determination or k-anonymity would be semantically wrong here, since no record-level suppression was performed — the material arrives deidentified from ATCC and HipSci. Scored 1 on that basis; the failure to cite the providers' deidentification/consent basis is raised as a medium-severity consistency issue rather than treated as absence.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition fails on evidence external to Element 4: description and keywords (E1) name cell lines, treatments and assays with no participant, patient or clinical-research reference, and collection_mechanisms (E8) describe laboratory instrumentation rather than recruitment. Per the per-sub-element gate, the governance disjunct does not reach sub-elements 3-5: a Data Access Committee over a dataset with no participants does not create participants whose privacy could be protected.
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy absent; no reidentification_risk assessment. The nearest statement, sensitive_elements: 'CM4AI data are non-clinical, derived from tissue cultures, and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject', concerns material rather than participants.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator: there are no participants whose privacy this sub-element could assess, so scoring 0 would measure the dataset's subject matter rather than its documentation.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same external determination: E1 description/keywords reference cell lines and assays, not participants or clinical research; E8 collection_mechanisms describe SEC-MS, AP-MS, ICC-IF and CRISPRi screening, not human recruitment; direct_collection.is_direct is false. The governance disjunct does not extend to this participant-scoped sub-element.
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent absent. Upstream donor consent is referenced only indirectly, via the HipSci MTA note in human_subject_research.notes.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator: no participants were enrolled by this dataset's producers, so there is no consent process of theirs to document. (Documenting the upstream donor-consent basis of the two cell lines would nonetheless strengthen the deidentification claim, and is recommended under sub-element 2.)

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same external determination from E1 description/keywords and E8 collection_mechanisms; no human participants were recruited or compensated. The governance disjunct does not extend to this participant-scoped sub-element.
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations and participant_compensation both absent. sampling_strategies.source_data records donor attributes of the source lines ('a 51-year-old black female with a metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma'; 'a healthy male Northern European donor') as provenance, not as a participant population.
sub_elements.quality_note: Excluded from the denominator: with no enrolled participants there is no at-risk population to protect and no compensation to report.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations: subpopulation_elements_present: true, identification by cell type and treatment condition (MDA-MB-468 untreated / paclitaxel / vorinostat; KOLF2.1J undifferentiated, NPC, neuron, cardiomyocyte), with a distribution statement mapping each modality onto the conditions it covers; subsets: seven entries each with an id, name, description and is_subpopulation: true
sub_elements.quality_note: The 'cohort' here is a matrix of cell lines by treatment and differentiation state, and it is described exhaustively and at the right granularity, including which assay covers which cell.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The subsets enumeration matches the subpopulations.distribution prose and matches the file_collections: AP-MS archives exist only for the two treated MDA-MB-468 conditions, exactly as stated. Consistent.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: instances: '464 proteins of interest imaged per treatment condition in MDA-MB-468 cells'; 'transcriptional and fitness phenotypes associated with 11,739 targeted genes'; sampling_strategies: '100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes'; total_file_count: 10; file_collections carry per-archive sizes (3.8 GB, 4.6 GB, 4.2 GB, 113.3 KB ...)
sub_elements.quality_note: Specific, modality-appropriate counts rather than a single headline number, and the record is explicit about the count it cannot give ('The bundle states the number of targeted genes; it does not state the number of profiled cells').
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The 464 figure is used identically in instances, subpopulations.distribution and three file_collections descriptions, and the record reconciles it against a conflicting 563 in an older release page. Project-level aggregates are deliberately kept out of the slot values. Consistent.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata, Tabular Flag, and Data Splits
sub_elements.evidence: is_tabular: false; subsets: seven entries with is_subpopulation: true; instances[].notes describing the four-channel image structure ('protein of interest (green), nucleus stained with DAPI (blue), endoplasmic reticulum stained with a calreticulin antibody (yellow), and microtubules stained with a tubulin antibody (red)')
sub_elements.quality_note: Two of the composite's signals are populated and informative — the tabular flag and seven flagged subpopulation subsets — and image channel semantics are documented, so the structural shape of the release is legible.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Partial: `variables` is absent (scored 0 at Element 3 sub-element 4) and no is_data_split flag appears, which is semantically correct since the release defines no train/test partition. is_tabular: false is flagged in source_caveats as inferred rather than stated, a minor provenance weakness. Scored 1 on the populated signals; the missing data dictionary is penalised once, at Element 3.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented

strengths: Identifier, publisher, citation and access path are mutually consistent: DOI 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, publisher ROR:0153tk833, a Dataverse access URL on the matching domain, and a ready-to-paste citation naming the same DOI and repository.

Funding transparency is exemplary — NIH awards 1OT2OD032742-01 and 5U54HG012513-02 with core project number, application ID, project period, PI and award amount, all following valid NIH construction, plus institutional support acknowledged.

Collection and acquisition are documented at reproducible granularity: named laboratories, per-channel immunofluorescence reagents, the 10x Genomics 3'HT readout, a 6-guide-per-gene CRISPRi library with inducible dCas9, and HPA antibody quality scoring.

Applicability determinations are unusually easy to make from external evidence: the description and collection mechanisms establish that no human participants were involved, while a named Data Access Committee, two named ethics contacts and a governance contact establish that oversight nonetheless exists.

Provenance is layered and checkable — raw deposits in MassIVE, SRA and Figshare, RO-Crate provenance graphs via FAIRSCAPE, per-file MD5 checksums, and four prior release DOIs linked with typed relationships.
The record documents its own evidentiary limits in source_caveats, adjudicating conflicting figures (464 versus 563 proteins) and conflicting affiliations rather than silently picking one.
weaknesses: No software is named for producing or transforming the files actually distributed: the richly documented node2vec / DenseNet-121 / HiDeF / GPT-4 pipeline produces cell maps the record states are not in this release, and FAIRSCAPE only packages it.
The `variables` slot is absent entirely, so the SEC-MS, AP-MS and Perturb-seq result tables ship without a data dictionary, column identifiers or units.
Version numbering is contradictory — this June 2026 release is '2.0' while the June and October 2025 releases are listed at '2.1', and the citation says 'V2'.
No errata and no per-release change description, so what this release adds relative to doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM must be inferred by diffing records.
No anomalies or missing-data documentation; the only quality statement reports QC as unfinished 'at the time of the CM4AI preprint' rather than as an outcome for the released files.

Only the ZIP container and its MIME type are declared; the formats and encodings of the files inside the archives are nowhere stated, and the `download_url` slot is left empty while the access link sits in distribution_formats.access_urls.
recommendations: Name, with versions, the software that produced each distributed collection — the mass-spectrometry search and SEC elution-profile tools behind the SEC-MS and AP-MS archives, and the alignment/quantification stack behind cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_cell_atlas.zip — keeping the cell-map pipeline clearly labelled as producing outputs not in this release.

Add `variables` entries with identifiers, descriptions and units for the columns of each tabular result file, and declare inner file formats and character encodings per file collection alongside the existing ZIP/RO-Crate declarations.

Reconcile the release version sequence (or state that Dataverse 'V2' and the CM4AI release version are separate numbering systems) and add release notes in updates.update_details enumerating what changed since the October 2025 release.

Populate `anomalies` and `missing_data_documentation` with per-modality quality outcomes — failed or low-scoring antibodies, low-confidence elution profiles, dropped guides, batch effects — and update cleaning_strategies from 'undergoing QC' to the QC result for the released files.
